tasks.name: Search ordered data with explicit boundaries
Search monotonic boundaries and answer spaces
Use sorting and ordered scans deliberately

concepts.name: Exact binary search
concepts.description: Search ordered data by comparing the midpoint and discarding the half that cannot contain the target.

concepts.name: Boundary binary search
concepts.description: Search for the first/last position satisfying a monotonic condition while preserving a candidate interval invariant.

concepts.name: Binary-search interval and progress
concepts.description: Keep interval semantics explicit and update boundaries so the candidate region strictly shrinks without discarding possible answers.

concepts.name: Binary search on answer space
concepts.description: Search a numeric or ordered answer domain when a feasibility predicate changes monotonically from false to true or true to false.

concepts.name: Sort to expose structure
concepts.description: Pay sorting cost when ordered data makes later comparisons, grouping, merging, or scanning substantially simpler.

concepts.name: Sort key and comparator contract
concepts.description: Choose a sort key/comparison that matches the problem's intended ordering without discarding required metadata.

concepts.name: Stable ordering
concepts.description: Preserve prior relative order among equal-key records when tie order is part of the contract or a multi-stage sort.

concepts.name: Ordered merge scan
concepts.description: Combine or compare sorted sequences by advancing only the frontier that can produce the next ordered result.

questions.prompt: A sorted array contains monotonically increasing sequence numbers. You need the index of sequence number 42017 or `-1` if absent. Which approach best uses the existing order?
questions.explanation: Exact binary search compares the midpoint and discards the half proven unable to contain the target, giving logarithmic comparisons.
hints: The data is already sorted, and the query asks for one exact key.

error_codes.description: The selected approach does not best exploit the existing sorted order for one exact lookup.

choice_feedback.binary: Correct: sorted order justifies halving the candidate interval.
choice_feedback.linear: Linear scan works but ignores the ordering information.
choice_feedback.sort: The data is already sorted; sorting again adds unnecessary work.
choice_feedback.hash: A hash map could help repeated exact lookups if built ahead of time, but for this one lookup the sorted structure already supports logarithmic search without extra O(n) state.

questions.prompt: The search uses an inclusive interval `[left, right]` and `mid = (left + right) // 2`. Flag the update that can fail to shrink the interval when `mid == left`.
questions.explanation: `left = mid` may leave the left boundary unchanged. If `values[mid] < target`, mid is already ruled out, so `left = mid + 1` is the progress-preserving update.
hints: Try a two-element interval.
